title: Who Works the Land?
description: How agricultural employment is distributed around the world — and how it has shifted over the past three decades.

items.label: The Wealth-Density Inversion
items.note: Out of every 1,000 workers, Burundi relies on 851 for farming. The United States needs just 10 — mechanisation does the rest.

items.label: Continental Dominance
items.note: Asia and Africa together account for over 68% of all global farming labour.

items.label: The Productivity Factor
items.note: Shifts out of agriculture are driven by better wages in services and manufacturing, plus improved seeds, tools, and irrigation freeing workers to move.

sections.heading: Agricultural Workforce Density by Region (per 1,000 Workers)
sections.caption: How many out of every 1,000 employed people work in agriculture, by region. All figures use the employed workforce — not total population — as the denominator.

sections.heading: Agricultural Share of Employment by Geography
Historical Decline in Agricultural Labour Density (1990 vs 2025)
sections.caption: Agricultural workers per 1,000 employed, comparing 1990 baseline to 2025. South Asia fell sharply; sub-Saharan Africa declined more slowly.
